A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MILD study. Their text, equations, Figure 1, Tables 1–4, and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification and MMLU routing experiments in Tables 1–3, plus severe expert-imbalance experiments in Appendix C.3 and Table 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds numerical comparisons with additional routing baselines, a margin-selection ablation, and robustness experiments in Sections 6.1–6.2.

M1.justification: The cost-sensitive reformulation, margin-dependent surrogate, theoretically guided margin selection, and MILD routing procedure remain unchanged. The restored sample summation in Section 5.3 agrees with the empirical expectation already stated in v1; it does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, Tiny ImageNet, and the same mathematics/history MMLU coverage. Section 6.2 extends MMLU evaluation to imperfect cost estimates and a cost-induced 95%/5% expert-imbalance scenario, without adding datasets or domains.

E2.justification: The MMLU comparison expands substantially beyond TDEF to Standard CE, Class-Weighted CE, and LDAM. Section 6.1 reports their error-plus-cost losses as 0.985, 0.942, and 0.915, respectively, against MILD's 0.813. These are evaluated alternatives, whereas v1 only discussed alternative approaches.

E3.justification: Section 6 revises the stated vision predictor from ResNet-16 to ResNet-18, without saying experiments were rerun. New analyses introduce uniform/theoretical/tuned margin controls, 20% Gaussian cost-matrix perturbations, and skewed inference costs. Existing metrics, training budgets, and documented test-set size remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 6.2 tests whether theoretical margin initialization helps independently of tuning, whether noisy cost estimates degrade routing, and whether minority routing survives extreme MMLU imbalance. These substantially extend the earlier analyses; Appendix C.3's severe image-expert imbalance experiment and C.4's tuning discussion are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over five runs and omit standard deviations for deferral ratios. New results follow the existing reporting practice. No additional seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results, but Sections 6.1–6.2 add substantial findings. Uniform/theoretical/tuned margins yield losses of 0.884/0.822/0.813; noisy-cost losses are 0.826 for MILD versus 1.054 for TDEF; extreme-imbalance losses are 0.885 versus 0.950. Additional CE, CWCE, and LDAM results broaden the comparative evidence.

T1.justification: Section 5.3 restores the missing sum over training examples in the displayed objective. Appendix G corrects an equality to an inequality when replacing a maximum of exponentials with their sum. These are local mathematical corrections; the principal assumptions, theorem statements, and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution paragraph, and conclusion are unchanged in substance and wording. They retain the same claims about the cost-sensitive reformulation, margin guarantees, MILD, and empirical benefits.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of margin-driven expert selection, distinguishes controlled vision imbalance from natural MMLU imbalance, and attributes robustness to margin buffering. It also asserts negligible offline estimation cost, identical scaling across expert sizes, and that the ablation proves the theoretical bound drives success. These extend interpretation beyond v1, sometimes beyond the demonstrated evidence.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses 4,000 MMLU router-training queries, revises the vision model specification, and supplies settings for the added margin and noise experiments. The training count is additional documentation, not evidence of increased training data. Baseline adaptations, the precise noise construction, and extreme-scenario cost values remain incompletely specified.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds recent work on online, expert-conditioned, and nonstationary deferral, alongside additional consistency and balanced-classification references, while dropping the multitask example and replacing the cited robustness work. Section 6.2 expands positioning against LDAM and temperature scaling. Numerous other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 adds an intuitive explanation and Section 6.2, moves and expands the standard cost-sensitive discussion from Appendix D, and makes localized grammatical and heading corrections. It also corrects Appendix H's theorem reference. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and all four tables are retained. Table 3 moves from page 8 to page 9; Tables 1–2 reposition subtable labels and refine captions, while equations and surrounding text reflow. The new experimental findings appear in prose rather than new figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons and controlled analyses strengthen empirical support, and the objective and Appendix G corrections improve mathematical clarity. The gain is limited by incomplete specifications for the new experiments and overstrong causal and scaling interpretations. Overall, v2 provides more useful evidence without substantially resolving these documentation and interpretation weaknesses.
